content:
mason: Heads up — Novara Health wants a special payment plan for a 3yr reserved commit. Asking for Net120 with 20% annual upfront and milestone invoicing for each year. Discount request: 25% off list.

olivia: do we have precedent for net120 on healthcare deals? sounds long. what's the ARR and why Net120?

mason: deal size ~ $1.2M ARR equivalent over the term (~$3.6M total). customer procurement is slow (hospital consortium), they require longer payment cycles. They want invoices split: 20% upfront annually, then 4 milestone invoices per year tied to deployment & security signoff.

priya_finance: Net120 is high risk. need AR aging impact and credit check. can we ask for a higher upfront (30%) or a short-term escrow? Also need GL code and order of invoices.

mason: customer pushed back on higher upfront. said budget cycles only allow that cadence. escrow was mentioned as an option but they'd prefer standard invoicing.

@deal-desk-bot: Please include: customer legal entity name, billing contact, tax status, and proposed invoice schedule. Attach credit check & reason for exception.

mason: quick details: Customer legal: Novara Health Inc; billing contact: procurement@novara.health; tax exempt: no; reason: hospital procurement cycles and central finance. Credit reference: provided three refs, awaiting completed form.

james_legal: for Net120 we need late payment interest and a payment plan in the SOW. also add termination-for-nonpayment clause and a data-hold/backcharge clause. if they want milestone invoices, define acceptance criteria per milestone.

priya_finance: run numbers: exposure if last invoice delayed 120 days = ~$600k receivable at any time. Recommend either Net90 + 30% upfront or Net120 with 40% annual upfront and bank guarantee.

ashley_csm: ops note — deployment windows align to their fiscal Qs; milestone acceptance will be product + security signoff, so we can define those as gating. CSM will own the acceptance checklist.

olivia: can we propose compromise in email to customer: Net90, 25% upfront annually, invoices quarterly; or Net120 but with 30% upfront + bank guarantee? Which option do we want Deal Desk to present?

mason: prefer to keep customer engaged — propose we offer the Net120 + 30% upfront + bank guarantee as alternative 1, and Net90 + 25% upfront as alternative 2. ask Deal Desk for approval to present both.

@deal-desk-bot: Recording request: exception type = Payment Terms; requested by = mason; customer = Novara Health Inc; value = $3.6M; term = 36 months; options = ["Net120 + 30% upfront + bank guarantee", "Net90 + 25% upfront"].

priya_finance: I can sign off on Net120 option only if bank guarantee or insurance is in place. Otherwise Net90 + 25% upfront gets my approval.

james_legal: can approve contract language edits for either option — will prepare milestone definitions and the payment security clause.

olivia: ok — @mason please send the two-option email to procurement with clear asks, cc finance & legal. @deal-desk-bot can you escalate for final sign-off? :thumbsup:

mason: will send within the hour. attaching proposed invoice schedule below:

```
Yearly Commit: $1,200,000
Option A (Net120 + 30% upfront + bank guarantee):
  - Invoice 1 (upfront): 30% = $360,000 on contract execution
  - Quarterly milestone invoices: 4x = $210,000 each, payable Net120
Option B (Net90 + 25% upfront):
  - Invoice 1 (upfront): 25% = $300,000 on contract execution
  - Quarterly invoices: adjusted to remaining balance, payable Net90
```

mason: tagging final: @priya_finance @james_legal @deal-desk-bot — request approval to present both options to Novara.

@deal-desk-bot: Escalation created to Deal Desk queue #DD-8721. Expected SLA 48h.

priya_finance: noted. I'll complete credit check and confirm risk tolerances by EOD tomorrow.

james_legal: I'll draft the milestone acceptance language and payment security clause, share a redline in this thread.

olivia: thanks team — leaning toward getting the bank guarantee in place, but appreciate the two-option approach.

mason: thanks all — will update after procurement reply. :pray:"
